quickAnswer: Kurban Bayramı travel in Turkey brings the country's largest domestic holiday migration. In 2026, the four-day festival runs May 27–30 following the May 26 half-day eve. State museums open at 13:00 on Day 1, the Grand Bazaar closes, coastal resort rates surge, and routine outpatient clinics pause while emergency departments stay open 24/7.

body.text: At [Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/), our two founders manage independent, client-paid, flat-fee travel, business, and medical travel planning across Türkiye. Paid by our clients. Independent of provider commissions. For medical visitors traveling near holiday dates: We coordinate your visit. Your licensed medical team makes clinical decisions.
What stays open vs closed on Day 1–4 of Kurban Bayramı?

On Day 1 of Kurban Bayramı (Wednesday, [May 27, 2026](https://vakithesaplama.diyanet.gov.tr/dinigunler.php?yil=2026)), state museums open at 13:00, banks and government offices close for all four days, and the Grand Bazaar and Spice Bazaar shut completely. On Days 2 through 4 (May 28–30), museums, malls, and most restaurants run standard hours.

Per [Ministry of Culture and Tourism holiday protocols](https://muze.gov.tr/duyuru-detay?Id=160), major archaeological sites such as Ephesus, Pamukkale, and Topkapı Palace welcome visitors from 13:00 on Day 1. Meanwhile, the [Grand Bazaar and Spice Bazaar](https://clevertourists.com/resources/istanbul-grand-bazaar-hours-guide) remain closed across the religious holiday, and local banks close from Tuesday afternoon (May 26) until Monday morning (June 1).
How do coastal resort prices and airport crowds spike?

Because Kurban Bayramı 2026 falls in warm late May ([May 27–30](https://diyanet.gov.tr/dini-gun-geceler)), coastal demand surges dramatically across Bodrum, Çeşme, Marmaris, Fethiye, Kaş, and Antalya. Hotels frequently enforce 4-to-5-night minimum stays and raise nightly rates by 40% to 100% compared with the previous week.

Istanbul (IST/SAW), Bodrum (BJV), Dalaman (DLM), and Antalya (AYT) terminals experience peak congestion on Tuesday afternoon (May 26) and Sunday afternoon (May 31). Highway corridors linking Istanbul and Ankara to the Aegean and Mediterranean coasts slow significantly during outbound and return waves.
Which cities remain calm for international visitors?

Istanbul, Ankara, and Bursa become noticeably calmer on Day 1 and Day 2 as millions of residents depart for coastal resorts and rural hometowns. Istanbul's residential neighborhoods—such as Nişantaşı, Bebek, and Moda—feel unusually relaxed, with lighter weekday-style traffic and easy Bosphorus walks.
To make the most of a Kurban Bayramı itinerary without fighting coastal bottlenecks, follow this logistics checklist:

items: Invert the domestic flow: Spend Kurban Bayramı days in Istanbul, then fly to the Aegean or Mediterranean coast on Monday after residents return home.
Book domestic flights 3+ months ahead: Lock in May 26–31 flights early before economy buckets sell out.
Avoid coastal driving on May 26 and May 31: Use morning flights or shift road transfers by 24 hours.
Reserve Bosphorus and Beyoğlu dining early: Popular waterfront restaurants still fill up on Days 2 and 3.
Allow extra airport security time: Arrive at domestic terminals at least 2 hours before departure during holiday waves.

body.text: How do clinic and hospital schedules adjust during Bayram?

Public hospital outpatient clinics (poliklinikler) and most private dental, aesthetic, and specialist practices close during Kurban Bayramı, while emergency departments (acil servis) at both public and JCI-accredited private hospitals remain fully staffed 24/7. Pharmacies operate on a rotating duty schedule (nöbetçi eczane) posted on every pharmacy door.

International patients planning elective procedures should avoid scheduling surgery between May 26 and May 31, 2026, because follow-up diagnostics, lab turnaround, and post-op clinic visits are harder to coordinate on holiday rosters. faq.q: What are the official 2026 Kurban Bayramı dates in Türkiye?
faq.a: According to [Diyanet](https://vakithesaplama.diyanet.gov.tr/dinigunler.php?yil=2026), Arefe (half-day eve) is Tuesday, May 26, 2026, and the four official holiday days run Wednesday, May 27 through Saturday, May 30, 2026.

faq.q: Will travelers witness animal sacrifice in tourist areas?
faq.a: No. Turkish municipal regulations restrict ritual sacrifice to designated licensed municipal facilities away from historic districts, hotels, and central tourist streets.

faq.q: Are Cappadocia hot air balloons operating during Kurban Bayramı?
faq.a: Yes. Balloon flights operate every morning weather permits, though baskets sell out early due to heavy domestic holiday bookings.

faq.q: Can I exchange currency or use ATMs during Kurban Bayramı?
faq.a: ATMs and card terminals work normally, and exchange offices in central tourist zones (such as Taksim and Sultanahmet) generally stay open on Days 2–4, though banks remain closed.

faq.q: Is public transportation affected in Istanbul during Kurban Bayramı?
faq.a: Metros, trams, Marmaray, and ferries operate on holiday schedules throughout all four days, providing reliable transit across the city.
